title: Feature-flag consumption segmentation playbook
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook describes how we map feature-flag-driven product features to consumption segments, routing policies, and pricing envelopes. It is intended for Product Managers, Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, and Backend Engineers responsible for packaging, rollout, and telemetry.

Purpose
-------
- Provide a repeatable process to translate new LLM-driven features behind feature flags into predictable consumption buckets.
- Reduce billing surprises for customers by exposing deterministic mapping from flag state -> consumption tier.
- Enable safe rollouts (canary, ramp, rollback) with observability and pricing guardrails.

Background
----------
Redwood supports many client-visible features that materially change token usage (e.g., session anchoring, long-context retrieval, multimodel orchestration). Historically customers were surprised when enabling these features increased per-session cost. Feature-flag consumption segmentation aims to:
1) measure expected incremental consumption for a feature,
2) assign the feature to a pricing segment or requirement (quota, credit, reserved commit), and
3) provide rollout guidance and telemetry hooks.

Definitions
-----------
- Consumption segment: a named bucket that defines expected per-request compute and billing behavior (e.g., micro, standard, heavy).
- Exposure factor: multiplier applied to baseline token usage to estimate delta when a flag is on.
- Feature flag contract: the documented mapping between feature states and corresponding consumption segment and pricing expectations.

High-level workflow
-------------------
1. Feature proposal (PM) includes a draft "consumption sketch" with expected exposure factor, example workloads, and anchor customers.
2. Lab evaluation (Applied ML/Optimize) runs a synthetic workload to validate exposure factor and produces a perf/latency/cost profile.
3. Pricing mapping (Product + Finance) chooses a consumption segment and billing treatment.
4. Implementation (Eng) wires flags to routing and quota systems and emits telemetry hooks.
5. Canary rollout (SRE + Product) validates real-world consumption and refines pricing mapping.
6. Graduate or rollback depending on outcome.

Design and artifacts
--------------------
Every feature must produce the following artifacts before a public rollout:
- Feature Flag Contract (markdown) describing states and default segment mapping.
- Consumption Test Harness (JSON/YAML) to replay typical tenant traffic for profiling.
- Telemetry contract: list of metrics the runtime must emit when the flag is present.
- Billing rule: routing to segment-specific meters/quotas or note for manual reconciliation.

Example Feature Flag Contract (template)
---------------------------------------
Title: Conversational-KV-enhanced-completions
Owner: eng-serving-runtime + product
States:
- off: baseline model, routing to segment: standard
- kv_on: prefetching + KV lookup + extra tokens, routing to segment: heavy
Exposure estimates:
- median token delta: +120 tokens per call
- 95th percentile delta: +420 tokens per call
Suggested billing treatment: auto-assign to "heavy" consumption segment; customers on per-token plans billed at standard rates but SRE adds a monitoring alert threshold after 24 hours of >15% revenue variance.

Consumption test harness example (YAML)
--------------------------------------
workload_name: kv_prefetch_sim
requests_per_minute: 1200
average_session_length: 9
input_distribution: conversational
variants:
  - baseline_model: redwood-alpha-1
  - kv_enabled: redwood-alpha-1 + kv-prefetch

Telemetry contract (minimum metrics)
- flag.feature_name.active_count: gauge (number of requests with flag enabled)
- feature.token_delta.p50/p95: histogram (difference in input+output tokens vs baseline)
- feature.latency.p50/p95: histogram (end-to-end time with flag enabled)
- feature.error_rate: counter (errors attributable to the feature codepath)
- feature.impact.revenue_estimate_hourly: gauge (approx incremental spend estimate)

Pricing mapping guidance
-----------------------
We use three canonical consumption segments for feature-flag mapping: micro, standard, heavy. Mapping rules:
- micro: exposure factor < 1.05 and < 20 token delta p95.
- standard: exposure factor between 1.05 and 1.5 or token delta p95 between 20 and 200.
- heavy: exposure factor > 1.5 or token delta p95 > 200.
Exceptions: features that introduce non-token compute (e.g., external calls, expensive rerankers) must be evaluated as "heavy" by default and an engineering cost-breakdown provided.

Decision matrix (text table)
- Feature characteristic | Default mapping
- Low token delta & stateless | micro
- Moderate delta or caching | standard
- High delta / external compute / multimodel | heavy

Billing treatments
------------------
- Auto-segment assignment: The runtime tags requests for customers who have enabled the flag. Tagged requests are billed via the segment meter and appear as separate line items on invoices.
- Quota gating: If a feature would exceed a customer's quota tier, the runtime can be configured to either reject requests, downgrade to baseline behavior, or queue the request for manual approval.
- Reserved commit adjustments: For committed Dedicated customers, we provide a committed-reserve delta estimation and a one-time migration credit to offset initial rollover risk.

Rollout playbook (numbered steps)
--------------------------------
1. Internal rollout: enable feature flag for internal org only; run consumption harness for 72 hours.
2. Canary tenants: pick 3 partner tenants across small/medium/large tiers and enable for 48–96 hours.
3. Observe telemetry and billing deltas; check for regressions in latency and error_rate.
4. Finance review: estimate monthly revenue delta and propose a pricing notice if expected to change >10% per tenant.
5. Public soft-launch: enable flag for 5% of new signups for 14 days.
6. Full launch: flip the default on for the segment after stakeholder signoff.
7. Post-launch 30/90-day review: confirm telemetry, SLA impacts, and invoice reconciliation.

Rollback criteria
-----------------
- Sustained token delta 10x higher than lab estimate for >2 hours.
- Error_rate increase > 1% absolute or > 2x baseline for >30 minutes.
- Latency p95 regression that violates target SLO for the impacted tier (see SLO section).

SLOs assumed for mapping
------------------------
- Latency p50 (feature path) <= 200ms for micro/standard segments, <= 400ms for heavy segment (non-blocking workloads).
- Error rate (feature path) < 0.5% by default.
- Billing estimation accuracy: within ±15% of realized incremental spend during the first 14 days of canary for 75% of canaries.

Telemetry and dashboarding requirements
--------------------------------------
- Product must publish a feature landing page with: flag contract, expected segment, lab profile summary, and link to real-time dashboard.
- Engineering must add feature-specific panels to the per-feature telemetry dashboard: token delta histograms, latency percentiles, customer-level revenue delta table.
- Alerts: automated alert when per-customer hourly incremental_spend > $1000 or when aggregate revenue_delta > 15% vs forecast.

Engineering implementation notes
------------------------------
- Runtime tagging: introduce header X-Redwood-Feature-Segment: <segment> which the billing pipeline consumes.
- Sampling: if telemetry volume is high, sample 1 in N requests but ensure histograms can be reconstructed. Use deterministic sampling keyed by tenant_id to avoid bias.
- Safe downgrade: implement a runtime flag to force baseline behavior for a tenant (override via console and API).

CLI examples and config snippet
----------------------------
# Enable feature for a tenant (SRE/Customer Success)
redwoodctl feature enable --tenant t-1234 --feature conversational-kv --state kv_on

# Force baseline for a tenant (emergency)
redwoodctl feature override --tenant t-1234 --feature conversational-kv --state off --reason "latency spike"

JSON billing tag example emitted by runtime:
{
  "tenant_id": "t-1234",
  "request_id": "r-abc-567",
  "feature_segment": "heavy",
  "token_delta_estimate": 182
}

Finance and commercial notes
---------------------------
- Pricing communication: For features mapped to heavy, Sales must surface the expected cost delta in commercial negotiations and include a sample invoice explanation.
- Credits: For large customers migrating features, Finance may approve a one-time credit equal to 25% of the first-month projected delta (case-by-case).
- Metering audit: Billing must reconcile the runtime tags against usage tables during initial 30-day post-launch and report discrepancies >2%.

Edge cases and appendices
------------------------
- Multimodel pipelines: When a single feature enables N backend models, the exposure factor should be computed per-model and then summed. Document the per-model weight in the contract.
- Privacy-sensitive features: If feature telemetry includes PII, redact at source and only emit aggregated metrics. Mark the feature contract confidentiality: restricted.

Frequently asked questions
--------------------------
Q: Who owns the final pricing decision for a feature?
A: Product proposes the segment; Finance signs off on customer-facing pricing treatment.

Q: What if a customer refuses higher pricing for a heavy feature?
A: We provide downgrade paths (turn feature off, or queue requests) and migration credits during transition.
